first_frame: A person holding a phone with a tempered glass screen protector, about to hit it with a hammer.
beats: 0-3 s: Hook: Hammering a phone screen to grab attention.
3-10 s: Intro: Explaining the variety of tempered glasses in the market.
10-20 s: Problem/News: Introducing the new government BIS mandate for screen protectors.
20-30 s: Context: Why this matters (market size, cost implications).
30-45 s: Analysis: Discussing quality vs. price and the impact on consumers.
45-60 s: Deep Dive: How the mandate will affect manufacturing and imports.
60-78 s: Conclusion/CTA: Questioning the necessity of the mandate and asking for viewer input.
visual_techniques: Quick cuts between talking head and B-roll of screen protectors at 3s, 8s, 16s
Screen recordings of news articles at 12s, 20s, 45s, 48s
Screen recordings of e-commerce listings at 26s
Text overlays highlighting key figures (12,000-15,000 crore) at 13s
Picture-in-picture style for news articles at 45s
captions: Simple, bold white text with black outline, 3-5 words per chunk, centered, no specific highlight color.
sound: High-energy, fast-paced voiceover, upbeat background music, sound effects for hammer hits and transitions.
recurring_element: The host holding two different tempered glasses, using them as props throughout the video.
ending: CTA asking viewers for their thoughts and to subscribe.
why: The video starts with a high-stakes visual (hammering a phone) that immediately hooks the viewer. It then transitions into relevant, timely news (BIS mandate) that affects a wide audience (smartphone users). The host maintains a conversational tone, making complex policy changes easy to understand. The use of B-roll and screen recordings keeps the pacing fast and engaging.
reusable_faceless: Using a high-stakes visual hook at the start
Incorporating screen recordings of relevant news articles
Using text overlays to emphasize key data points
Keeping the pacing fast with frequent cuts
